proof: Neither side declares aspect-ratio. The draft's value is the INTRINSIC form `auto 48 / 22` (`auto 40 / 18` in the scrolled state) - the computed shape a replaced element takes when it has intrinsic dimensions - against live's bare `auto`, i.e. the live presents no intrinsic ratio. CR10 built the declared-aspect-ratio route, but `USED_VALUES` covers only `width`, so there is no intrinsic guard for aspect-ratio and nothing a setting writes could ever produce `auto 48 / 22`. The existing route therefore misses it not through a missing control but because the row's value is a used/intrinsic value: a measuring artefact whose real cause is markup (the logo carrying no width/height, or an uploaded SVG stripped of its viewBox).

proof: Zero SGS settings exist on any woocommerce/* block (Spec 47 section 2), and no enclosing SGS block can reach inside the product loop's own markup - sgs/container::maxWidth paints only its own wrapper. Live declares `max-width: 100%` on the product-template <ul> where the draft's <div> has the initial `none`, so only the theme's WooCommerce stylesheet can change it. Caveat: the pair also crosses element types (draft <div> -> live <ul>), so part of this row may dissolve once a tag-mismatch check exists.
